### Minor Changes - [#3196](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3196) [`b226ab9`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/b226ab91fab05803d351d0269cfd921aec3a7b7f) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Block diagram links ([#3105](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/3105)). `a --> b`, `a --- b`, `a ==> b`, `a -.- b`, the `x` / `o` / `<` markers and `a -- "text" --> b` now parse and draw. `parseBlock` returns the links as `BlockDiagram.edges` (`BlockEdge`), and `layoutBlock` returns them as `PositionedBlockDiagram.edges` with Mermaid 12.3.0's path points, basis-curve path and label place. `pnpm run block:oracle` now also compares every link's path and label place with real mermaid.js. The ASCII output leaves room between cells for links and draws each as a line with an arrow head. - [#3206](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3206) [`fd836f6`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/fd836f6d3a40a8104d00f920a820372b0fd43dc3) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Block diagram node shapes and block arrows ([#3106](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/3106)). `a(("x"))` circle, `a((("x")))` double circle, `a{"x"}` diamond, `a{{"x"}}` hexagon, `a(["x"])` stadium, `a[["x"]]` subroutine, `a[("x")]` cylinder, `a>"x"]` asymmetric, `a[/"x"/]` `a[\"x"\]` leaning boxes, `a[/"x"\]` `a[\"x"/]` trapezoids and `a<["x"]>(right, down)` block arrows now parse and draw as Mermaid 12.3.0 does: each shape's natural size, its second-pass geometry in a wider cell, and its own outline for link clipping. `BlockShape` grows the shape names, `BlockNode` gains `directions` and `PositionedBlockNode` gains `geometry`. The ASCII renderer gives each shape the delimiters the flowchart renderer uses. `pnpm run block:oracle` compares each shape's centre and circle radii, polygon points or cylinder path, and now scores a case per shape. - [#3199](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3199) [`16ec2be`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/16ec2be9f38245174166314273c31fac965967ef) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Block diagram styling and `block.padding` ([#3107](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/3107)). `classDef`, `class` and `style` now parse and apply as Mermaid 12.3.0 does: `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width` and the other properties go inline on the block's rectangle, `color` on its label, and a `style` item replaces the same property from a class. `block.padding` from front matter or `%%{init}%%` sets the space between cells and inside each block (default 8). `parseBlock` returns `classDefs` and `padding` on `BlockDiagram` and `classes` and `styles` on `BlockNode`; `PositionedBlockNode` gains `classes` and `css`; `InitConfig` gains `block.padding`. `pnpm run block:oracle` now also compares each block's inline styles. A markdown label is a parse error in Mermaid 12.3.0 (`Expecting 'STR', got 'MD_STR'`), so it stays an error here, with that message. - [#3128](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3128) [`2f0f7c3`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/2f0f7c3759b8293da359a4d3fb4a00f295746aa3) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Block diagrams. `block` and `block-beta` diagrams now parse and render to SVG and ASCII/Unicode text, under the upstream-types umbrella ([#2085](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2085), [#2805](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2805)). `DiagramType` gains `'block'` and `detectDiagramType` routes a `block` / `block-beta` header to it (case-sensitively, as Mermaid's detector does). `@zombie-mermaid/mermaid-parser` adds `parseBlock` with the `BlockDiagram`, `BlockNode` and `PositionedBlockDiagram` types, a port of Mermaid 12.3.0's lexer and database for `columns`, blocks (`id`, `id["text"]`, `id("text")`), `id:N` spans, `space`, and `block:id ... end` groups. `@zombie-mermaid/svg-renderer` adds `layoutBlock` and `renderBlockSvg`: Mermaid's grid layout, with label widths found by summing Trebuchet MS advances. `pnpm run block:oracle` compares every block, corner radius and the drawing size with real mermaid.js and agrees on all gallery samples with mermaid 12.3.0. The ASCII output is this library's own design (Mermaid has none): a grid of boxed cells with groups as larger boxes. Links, the other shapes and styling are rejected with an error naming a tracking issue ([#3105](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/3105), [#3106](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/3106), [#3107](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/3107)). Colours follow the theme (see `docs/known-differences.md`). - [#3125](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3125) [`053891a`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/053891a18f35ac05e8296c06b57bef24ee0b23fb) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Event modeling diagrams. `eventmodeling` is parsed, drawn to SVG and rendered to ASCII/Unicode text instead of being rejected with "Invalid mermaid header", under the upstream-types umbrella ([#2085](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2085), [#2806](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2806)). `DiagramType` gains `'eventmodeling'` and `detectDiagramType` routes an `eventmodeling` header to it (case-sensitively, as Mermaid's detector does). `@zombie-mermaid/mermaid-parser` adds `parseEventModeling` with the `EventModeling` and `Positioned*` types, a port of the grammar in `@mermaid-js/parser` 2.0.1 and the database in Mermaid 12.3.0: `tf`/`rf` frames and their long forms, the five entity types, `Namespace.Name` identifiers, `->>` source frames, inline data and `data` blocks, `entity`/`note`/`gwt` (parsed, not drawn) and Mermaid's errors (duplicate frame ID; `title` and `accTitle` are syntax errors). `@zombie-mermaid/svg-renderer` adds `layoutEventModeling` and `renderEventModelingSvg`: Mermaid's swimlane, box and arrow geometry, with text widths from Trebuchet MS bold advances. `pnpm run eventmodeling:oracle` compares every swimlane, box, arrow and the drawing size with real mermaid.js and agrees on all gallery samples with mermaid 12.3.0. The ASCII output is this library's own design (Mermaid has none): horizontal swimlane bands with time running left to right. Colours follow the theme except the entity fills (see `docs/known-differences.md`). - [#3124](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3124) [`6ab388d`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/6ab388da8dc1f126719eb9aad773c35b6721b3f9) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Add the Ishikawa (fishbone) diagram: `ishikawa` and `ishikawa-beta` are parsed, drawn to SVG and rendered to ASCII instead of being rejected with "Invalid mermaid header". The parser follows mermaid@12.3.0's grammar (the effect, then categories and causes by indentation, `%%` comments, `
` in labels, Mermaid's label sanitizing). The SVG uses Mermaid's geometry: bones slanted 82° and alternating above and below the spine, causes spaced evenly along their bone, nested causes hung from their parent (`pnpm run ishikawa:oracle` agrees on every sample and edge case: element order, text, bone vectors and y positions exactly, x positions and the frame within text-width tolerance); the ASCII output is this library's own, a fishbone on a character grid, as Mermaid has no text mode. Not drawn: the `handDrawn` look. New exports: `parseIshikawa` and the `Ishikawa*` types from the parser, `layoutIshikawa`, `renderIshikawaSvg`, `wrapIshikawaText` and `ISHIKAWA` from the SVG renderer, and `'ishikawa'` in `DIAGRAM_TYPES`. Output change for sources that began `ishikawa` (previously an error). Checked against mermaid@12.3.0. - [#3219](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3219) [`9592690`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/959269058a6265e4ad129ce25110eeb0b3ea1950) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Output change, SVG: the default font is now mermaid@12.3.0's own stack, `"trebuchet ms", verdana, arial, sans-serif`, and labels are sized with its measured per-character widths (regular and bold) instead of an Inter estimate, as pie already was. Every diagram type's label boxes move, by up to a few pixels for short text and more for wide capitals and digits; flowchart node sizes now match 12.3.0 exactly on the probes (`A[xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx]` is 192.3 wide, `Wait Idle Ready` stays on one line). The SVG no longer asks Google Fonts for Inter by default; pass `font: 'Inter'` (or `embedFont: 'subset'`) to keep Inter, which keeps the previous widths. The ASCII renderer keeps its Inter-based layout. New `MERMAID_FONT_STACK`, `isTrebuchetFont` and `setTrebuchetMetrics` exports in core ([#3217](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/3217)). - [#3186](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3186) [`9fffd14`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/9fffd14be999f996642a60baa82fc33c3aefefea) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Treemap: read the `treemap` config keys mermaid@12.3.0 reads (`padding`, `nodeWidth`, `nodeHeight`, `showValues`, `valueFormat` as a d3-format specifier, `diagramPadding`) and apply every `classDef` property mermaid does: label properties to the text (a `font-size` sets the header size and where a leaf's fit starts), the rest to the box. - [#3120](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3120) [`bfcfef1`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/bfcfef188dc4252b2e37ae8917c473bcc72d3319) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Add Mermaid `treemap-beta` / `treemap` diagrams: parser, an SVG renderer that ports d3-hierarchy's squarified layout (cell positions and the viewBox agree with mermaid@12.3.0 to 0.01px) and an ASCII tree list with share bars. Rows nest by indentation, `title` and `classDef` / `:::class` (fill, stroke, stroke-width, color) are read; the `treemap` init keys are not yet. - [#3133](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3133) [`9d0e5ee`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/9d0e5ee94f195949230e03643cd562620405a435) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Use case diagrams: `usecase-beta` (the only header mermaid@12.3.0 detects) now renders to SVG and ASCII. Actors, use cases (`Name`, `Name(label)`, `Name[label]`), `systemBoundary`, `direction`, associations with labels, `include`/`extend`/generalization and `note for` are supported; metadata, stereotypes, classes, `json` nodes, circle/cross markers and edge ids are rejected with a "not supported yet" error. `parseUsecase` and `usecaseToGraph` join `@zombie-mermaid/mermaid-parser`; `DiagramType` gains `'usecase'`, `NodeShape` gains the `usecase-*` shapes and an edge `triangle` terminator. - [#3212](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3212) [`c232043`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/c232043958de4407ba27c8e054f4ce0b70a407e8) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Use case diagrams read `@{ ... }` node metadata and `json` nodes, as mermaid@12.3.0 does. An actor takes `type: hollow|awesome` or `icon`, an actor or ellipse `business: true`, a `systemBoundary` `type: package`; `Name@{ ... }` on its own line sets them for a name declared elsewhere, and a body may span lines. `json Name @ { ... }` draws a key/value table that only `--`, `-->` and `<--` lines may join. `parseUsecase` returns `type`, `icon`, `business`, a boundary `type` and `jsonNodes`. ASCII draws the actor variants and the json table; it draws a package boundary and a business ellipse as plain frames and ellipses. - [#3130](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3130) [`6998b40`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/6998b400248c360a684f122ce0559ac6234d4e72) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Wardley maps (`wardley-beta`) render as SVG and as ASCII ([#2820](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2820)). The parser covers the whole mermaid@12.3.0 grammar (size, evolution stages, anchors, components with label offsets, build/buy/outsource/market, inertia, links with flow arrows and labels, evolve, pipelines, notes, annotations, accelerators and deaccelerators), and the SVG agrees with 12.3.0 to 0.01px on every gallery sample and 28 edge cases (`pnpm run wardley:oracle`). The ASCII output is this library's own: components on a visibility/evolution grid. `detectDiagramType` returns `'wardley'`, so `DIAGRAM_TYPES` and `DiagramType` gain a member and `Record` maps need an entry. Output change: `wardley-beta` was rejected with "Invalid mermaid header". - [#3195](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3195) [`f89cbf1`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/f89cbf167427ab98c99a9ce97d9e0b7edbf3ddbc) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Wardley maps read `themeVariables.wardley` (eleven colours) from a `%%{init}%%` directive or front matter, as mermaid 12.3.0 does ([#3126](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/3126)). The ASCII renderer sizes its grid from `size [w, h]` and moves a label by its `[dx, dy]` offset. `InitConfig` gains `wardleyTheme`, `WardleyMap` gains `theme`, and `WARDLEY_THEME_KEYS` is exported. The `wardley-beta` config keys are not read: mermaid 12.3.0 drops them from a directive too. ### Patch Changes - [#3221](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3221) [`2e16eb9`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/2e16eb9df96a480bb046df24658c40ef2a47e3cd) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Output change, ASCII: in a left-to-right or right-to-left diagram, a back edge whose two ends mermaid@12.3.0's layout puts a node apart on the cross axis now keeps them on separate rows, and runs on a row of its own with its riser beside the target, as mermaid draws it. Before, both ends snapped to one row, so the jog beside the source was as long as the riser. CI/CD Pipeline's `Fix & Retry` back to `Push Code` (the `ascii-feedback-edge-sibling-order` fork fix) is the case that changes. - [#3150](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3150) [`ffed39a`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/ffed39a2603259ef43138295c6bd1b91c53f4b28) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Output change, ASCII: in a top-down diagram, a composite state or subgraph with exactly two labelled exits, one straight down and one that jogs right, now puts both labels on the jog row, the straight one on its own stroke to the left. mermaid@12.3.0 draws the pair at one height in that order; before, the straight exit's label sat near its target, so the labels read in the other order and the gap under the cluster was taller. State: Composite States (`done` and `fail`) is the sample that changes. - [#3193](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3193) [`88cf6d0`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/88cf6d00b7364969c65e86291c946c459585af95) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Output change, ASCII: in a top-down diagram, two edges from one subgraph to a node straight below it, with no other exit from the subgraph, now leave the subgraph's bottom wall and enter the target's top face as two parallel strokes. mermaid@12.3.0 draws the pair that way; before, the second edge left the cluster's side wall and entered the target's side face. - [#3101](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3101) [`8d4b3e8`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/8d4b3e83a8c5bca97ce67ae00c05efb9c6e185db) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - ASCII: in a left-to-right or right-to-left flow, a decision with three ends on its entry face (the way in and two returns, as `G{Tests?}` in the Git Branching Workflow sample) gives each end its own cell, on the vertex and the two slants, as mermaid@12.3.0 draws it, instead of ending the arrowhead and both returns on one shared stem. Needs the ELK layout provider (registered by default in `zombie-mermaid`'s entry points). - [#3167](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3167) [`7c41af0`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/7c41af0c6edcba739fec7bec3dc77299c66a0687) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - ASCII: three edges between two decisions in a horizontal flow leave in the order GitHub's mermaid draws them, the reciprocal's stroke last instead of first. - [#3153](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3153) [`063d445`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/063d445e3de93ab323828bb9f4a29275b186b8f9) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - ASCII with the ELK layout provider (the CLI and the root entry): two flowcharts that crashed now render. A subgraph whose member has a self-loop drawn past its nodes, with another edge running beside the frame, no longer runs out of memory (the frame-gutter widening chased a wall that moved with it). A subgraph with its own `direction` and a lane group between its members no longer throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'start')`. - [#3108](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3108) [`68abaac`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/68abaacc88073779b079acf9653108a02f6d7987) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - ASCII: a labelled left-to-right edge into a decision that takes a face lane no longer throws in the label placement, and its label is drawn instead of dropped. - [#3147](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3147) [`818de6e`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/818de6e38fb92a4bf62a76fb526ca7d53d39e637) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - ASCII: with the ELK layout provider, a long edge out of a fan no longer has its bend pulled up beside its source when the run into its target would then go through the boxes between the two layers; before, the stroke ran across those boxes and overwrote their text. - [#3190](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3190) [`3e44861`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/3e448615896d8c1a310848b4e9624bd9e29ba23f) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Output change, ASCII: a gantt chart now shades `excludes` days with `·` (`,` in ASCII mode) on cells no bar covers, and draws the `todayMarker` as a `│` (`|`) column when the current date is inside the chart's range, like the SVG; the legend names both. Gantt: Weekday excludes and Statuses, milestone and weekends are the samples that change. - [#3129](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3129) [`01169d4`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/01169d476c757cc89318ca180afee28e4f7268e4) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - ASCII: a left-to-right or right-to-left flow with several edges leaving one cluster (the "Cluster Exit Siblings" samples) no longer re-runs the same bend-row search hundreds of times while it lays out; the result is unchanged, only faster (one such render dropped from minutes to under a second on a heavily loaded machine). - [#3148](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3148) [`29794c3`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/29794c347e5a12f0e2d005297740717db1f6d9d2) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - ASCII: when two or more labelled edges join the same two nodes, a label no longer lands on the cell an earlier sibling's label slid to and overwrites it (`n82` and `C5` printed as `n825`). The later label now avoids the earlier label where it is drawn. - [#3213](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3213) [`b54e480`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/b54e4806f7d4c79984215bf3e15bc706640dbcf6) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Output change, ASCII: in a left-to-right or right-to-left flow, a Z-shaped edge that has a gap to itself (or only strokes that share its end cell) now bends on the column ELK bends it on, measured from the start face to the end face, instead of the gap's middle column, as mermaid@12.3.0 draws it. Without a layout provider the output is unchanged. Changes under a provider in LR and RL: LR Bypass Edge In A Chain, Parallel Links (&), linkStyle: Color-Coded Edges, Text-Embedded Labels and the other gallery flowcharts whose Z bent mid-gap. - [#3227](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3227) [`35eca80`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/35eca8058c9987d55b8cff808b2e7bb7dd2d9c48) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Output change, ASCII: a lone Z route now bends at the middle of its gap, as mermaid@12.3.0 bends it, in a top-down or bottom-up diagram, and for the strokes out of a hub in a left-to-right or right-to-left one (where the layout bends it mid-gap). The fan-in strokes into a node and the fan-out strokes out of it used to bend at a third or two thirds of the gap. - [#3226](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3226) [`a0fa7a9`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/a0fa7a903eacf5315123761d62d841308db0c0ab) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Output change, ASCII: in a left-to-right or right-to-left diagram, a lone Z route (one that shares its gap with nothing it could merge with) now bends at the middle of the gap, where mermaid@12.3.0 bends it, instead of a third of the way across. The bend hint is read from a layout with mermaid's real node sizes, and only when it lands at the middle. Bypass edges in a chain and the strokes into a fan-in hub are the cases that change. - [#3147](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3147) [`e1836d4`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/e1836d434460e5e3a227593d85138c4cee2341cf) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - ASCII: a flowchart whose self-loop takes a long detour past rows no other path touches (a BT flowchart with an `n4 ==> n4` loop and nine edges) no longer throws `RangeError: Invalid array length`. The widening for a loop that shares a track with another edge added 2 to a row that had no height yet, which made the canvas height `NaN`. - [#3205](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3205) [`d207e98`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/d207e9889e05e02e75de0947416ccb9657b630f9) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Output change, ASCII: in a left-to-right or right-to-left flow, a node that ELK ends more than three edges on one side face (the hub of `ascii-longest-path-layering`, `Closed` in State: Connection Lifecycle) now grows a row per end, and each end takes a row of its own on that face in ELK's order, start then arrival of a reciprocal pair, with its own arrowhead, as mermaid@12.3.0 draws them. Back edges enter that face by the gutter instead of running along the node's wall, and a labelled reciprocal pair on a face of three ends or fewer no longer shares one cell. New hint: `AsciiEdgeHint.bend`, where ELK's route bends along the flow axis (0 beside the start face, 1 beside the end face). The ELK provider fills it. A Z-shaped edge in a horizontal flow bends on the side ELK does and puts its label on the long run on the other side. Without a provider the output is unchanged. State: Connection Lifecycle, `ascii-longest-path-layering`, `ascii-label-canvas-edge` and Dense Duplicate Edges change under a provider in LR and RL. - [#3121](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3121) [`cb7413b`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/cb7413b2e4b12413a110ffaabaa3b77cd3f55733) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - ASCII: in a left-to-right flow, the edge that skips a node (`A --> C` past `B`, with `A --> B --> C`) now leaves A's right face, runs along the border row on the side away from `B`, and rises (or drops) into C's left face, as mermaid@12.3.0 draws it, instead of running straight along the row. - [#3229](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/3229) [`73721eb`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/73721eb7645291127d4275e9bfac25403c0a2e32) Thanks [@dfadler](https://github.com/dfadler)! - Output change, ASCII: in a left-to-right or right-to-left diagram, a back edge whose run has to clear another stroke of its source now rises beside its target, and a forward edge across more than one layer drops beside its target, as mermaid@12.3.0 bends them (`Git Branching Workflow` pass return, `Edges Into and Out of Subgraphs` Cluster-to-Audit).
